 In The High Court At Calcutta
 Civil Appellate Jurisdiction
 Appellate Side

The Hon'ble Justice Ananya Bandyopadhyay
 F.M.A.T.(Mv) 1171 of 2019
 New India Assurance Company Limited
 vs
 Md. Sirajul Haque
For the Appellant : Mr. Parimal Kumar Pahari
For the Respondents : Mr. Ali Imam Shah
Heard & Judgment on : 06.05.2025

Ananya Bandyopadhyay, J.:-
1.
The instant appeal was heard earlier and judgment was reserved.
However, the matter was listed under the heading 'For Hearing' for further clarification.
2. The learned Advocates representing the appellant/insurance company as well as the respondents/claimants are present.

3. The instant appeal had been filed against the judgment and award dated 13.06.2019 passed by the learned Judge, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Fast Track Court, Suri, Birbhum in M.A.C. Case No.
92 of 2012.

entities.text: Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Fast Track Court, Suri, Birbhum
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 4. The claimant being the victim injured in the accident filed an application under Section 166 of the M.V. Act in the Court of Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Birbhum being MAC Case No. 92/2012 claiming an award of Rs.5,00,000/-.
5. The victim and his daughter were travelling in a bus bearing registration no. WB-19A/3571 which was hit by a truck being registration no. WB- 57/4585 in a rash and negligent manner.
6. As a result, the victim was grievously injured.
7. Subsequently, based on a complaint, Md. Bazar Police Station Case No. 78/05 dated 02.08.2005 was instituted against the driver of the offending vehicle.

sentences.text: The owner of the offending vehicle despite receiving summons failed to appear and the case proceeded ex parte against him.
9. The respondent, the New India Assurance Company Limited contested the aforesaid MAC Case.

10. The learned Tribunal as aforesaid disposed of the issues framed considering the oral as well as documentary evidences and allowed for Rs.8,40,840/- with an interest payable at 6% from the date of filing the application till realization of the amount.

11. The learned Advocate representing the appellant argued as follows:-
(a) The claimant did not suffer any loss of earning or earning capacity as he had been continuing with his services as a headmaster in a primary school drawing his full salary and was drawing pension after his retirement.
( b) There was no evidence to support that there has been any loss in income or earning capacity.

(c) The compensation was granted on the basis of a certificate by the Medical Board stating he was 50% disabled, however, the date of this certificate was issued in the year of 2017 while accident occurred in 2005, furthermore, the certificate did not narrate the history of disability.
(d) The claimant failed to prove medical expenses or future medical expenses incurred by him after the accident before the learned Tribunal.
He also failed to prove any loss of income and in such case the claimant was entitled to receive compensation under the heads of pain and suffering, loss and discomfort of life.
(e) When deciding the quantum of compensation, the learned Tribunal ought to have considered if the injuries caused by the accident resulted in loss of earning capacity and/or income.

(f) The following cases were relied on - (i) ACJ 2011 (1) Raj Kumar -Vs.- Ajay Kumar & Anr.
(ii) 2011 ACJ 2869 Sanjay Batham -Vs.- Munnalal Parihar & Ors.
(iii)2014 (4) TAC (Cal) Smt. Ashoka Mitra & Anr. -Vs.- Sri Nanku Gupta & Anr.
(iv) 2012 SAR (Civil) 733 Kavita -Vs.- Deepal & Ors.
12.
Heard the submissions of the learned advocates representing the respective parties.

sentences.text:
Since the occurrence of the accident, involvement of the offending vehicle, the driving license,
Insurance certificate etc. are not disputed by the learned advocate representing the respondents/insurance company, this Court restricts itself only to the extent of considering the aforementioned issues.
Perused the oral as well as documentary evidence on record and the reasons cited by the learned Tribunal in assessing the compensation awarded which in the opinion of this Court is justified.
The impugned Judgment and order is not interfered with.
14. The learned Advocate representing the appellant/Insurance Company submitted to have deposited a sum of Rs.14,02,567/- before the office of the learned Registrar General, High Court Calcutta.

15. The office of the Registrar General, High Court, Calcutta shall encash the said cheque and thereafter disburse the same to the respondent/claimant as mentioned in the award passed by the learned Judge, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Fast Track Court, Suri, Birbhum in M.A.C. Case No.
92 of 2012 on proof of proper identification of the respondent/claimant subject to payment of ad valorem Court's fees and refund the balance amount through a cheque to the Learned Advocate for the Appellant/Insurance Company for the accounts of the insurance company.

entities.text: Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Fast Track Court, Suri, Birbhum
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 16. The interest generated on the sum of money deposited by the appellant/insurance company at the office of the Learned Registrar General, High Court at Calcutta which has already been deposited in the nationalized bank by the office of the Learned Registrar General, High Court at Calcutta is to be apportioned and the sum of interest accrued on the aforesaid amount is to be disbursed in favour of the appellant/insurance company for the accounts of the insurance company.
17. The instant appeal is disposed of accordingly.
18. The pending applications, if any, stands disposed of.
19. Copy of the order be sent to the Department as well as the concerned tribunal as expeditiously as possible.

(Ananya Bandyopadhyay, J.) Srimanta, A.R. (Ct.)
